findings.title: Mutable default value: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`
findings.body: In a dataclass, a default value of `timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class definition time and is then shared by every instance created without an explicit `queued` argument. Every `AssignmentSource(source_name=..., integration_id=...)` constructed in a worker will therefore have the same `queued` datetime (the import time of the module), not the time the source was actually queued. The correct pattern is `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The field is not yet consulted in any comparison logic in this PR, so the cycle-breaking itself still works, but the field is serialized through Celery as `to_dict` / `from_dict` and any future use of `queued` for staleness, deduplication, or analytics will be incorrect. The test `test_to_dict` only asserts the key is present, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: Test name typo: `inalid_data`
findings.body: The test method is named `test_from_dict_inalid_data`. The intended spelling is `test_from_dict_invalid_data`. Renaming fixes a misleading test identifier that hides intent and breaks search/grep for invalid-input tests.

findings.title: No test catches the mutable-default bug for `queued`
findings.body: `test_to_dict` only asserts that `result.get("queued") is not None`. A test that constructs two `AssignmentSource` instances in sequence (e.g., with a short sleep between them) and asserts that `s1.queued != s2.queued` would have detected the shared-default bug in the dataclass. Add this assertion, plus a `from_dict` round-trip test, before relying on `queued` for any logic.

findings.title: `assignment_source.to_dict()` recomputed on every loop iteration
findings.body: In `sync_group_assignee_outbound`, the expression `assignment_source.to_dict() if assignment_source else None` is evaluated inside the `for external_issue_id in external_issue_ids` loop, so `to_dict()` (and therefore `asdict()` plus a full copy of the dataclass) is run once per linked external issue. The value does not depend on `external_issue_id`; compute it once before the loop and reuse the dict in the kwargs. The `AssignmentSource` is frozen, but the inner dict is rebuilt unnecessarily for each outbound task.

findings.title: Missing test for cross-integration propagation (cycle break must not over-block)
findings.body: The new `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` proves the loop is broken when the source equals the only target. It does not prove the other direction the PR's docstring relies on: when multiple integrations are linked to the same group, an inbound change from integration A must still propagate to integration B. Without a test that links two `ExternalIssue`s from two different provider integrations and asserts that `sync_assignee_outbound` IS called for the non-source one, the `should_sync` short-circuit could regress to blocking all outbound sync (e.g., by checking integration_id more broadly) and the suite would still pass.
